blocks.title: Read entity
blocks.description: Reads the state (or an attribute) of an HA entity.

blocks.title: Write entity
blocks.description: Writes the value to an HA entity with the matching service. Writes only when the value changes (with optional deadband and minimum interval).

params.name: data_key
params.label: Data field for the value
params.help: e.g. brightness (empty = no value is sent)

blocks.title: Setpoint (HA)
blocks.description: Creates a number entity in HA that can be adjusted from a dashboard, and outputs its value in the program.

blocks.title: Switch (HA)
blocks.description: Creates a switch entity in HA (e.g. a manual override) and outputs its state.

blocks.title: Publish value
blocks.description: Makes an internal signal available as a sensor/binary_sensor in HA (for dashboards, history and automations).

params.name: device_class
params.label: Device class (optional)
params.help: The HA name in lower case, e.g. temperature. Pick from the list or type it.

params.name: deadband
params.label: Deadband
params.help: Numbers are sent to HA only when they have changed at least this much. 0 = every change.

params.name: min_interval
params.label: Minimum interval (s)
params.help: At most one new value this often. The latest value always gets through.

blocks.title: Constant (number)
blocks.description: Fixed number.

blocks.title: Constant (on/off)
blocks.description: Fixed on/off value.

blocks.title: Comment
blocks.description: Free text on the drawing. Does not affect the logic.

blocks.title: AND
blocks.description: The output is on when all inputs are on.

blocks.title: OR
blocks.description: The output is on when at least one input is on.

blocks.title: XOR
blocks.description: The output is on when an odd number of inputs are on.

blocks.title: NOT
blocks.description: Inverts the input.

blocks.title: SR latch (set dominant)
blocks.description: Set/reset latch. Set wins when both are on. Kept over a restart.

blocks.title: RS latch (reset dominant)
blocks.description: Set/reset latch. Reset wins when both are on. Kept over a restart.

blocks.title: Rising edge
blocks.description: Gives one pulse (one scan) when the input goes from off to on.

blocks.title: Falling edge
blocks.description: Gives one pulse (one scan) when the input goes from on to off.

blocks.title: Toggle (impulse relay)
blocks.description: Every rising edge on the input toggles the output. Kept over a restart.

blocks.title: Greater than
blocks.description: The output is on when A > B.

blocks.title: Greater or equal
blocks.description: The output is on when A ≥ B.

blocks.title: Less than
blocks.description: The output is on when A < B.

blocks.title: Less or equal
blocks.description: The output is on when A ≤ B.

blocks.title: Equal
blocks.description: The output is on when A = B.

blocks.title: Not equal
blocks.description: The output is on when A ≠ B.

blocks.title: Hysteresis
blocks.description: On when input ≥ high, off when input ≤ low, otherwise unchanged.

blocks.title: In range
blocks.description: On when low ≤ input ≤ high.

blocks.title: Select (SEL)
blocks.description: Outputs in1 when g is on, otherwise in0.

blocks.title: Text equals
blocks.description: On when the text equals the given value (e.g. hvac mode 'heat').

blocks.title: Add
blocks.description: Sums the inputs.

blocks.title: Subtract
blocks.description: out = A − B

blocks.title: Multiply
blocks.description: Multiplies the inputs.

blocks.title: Divide
blocks.description: out = A ÷ B. Division by zero gives out 0 and err on.

blocks.title: Minimum
blocks.description: Lowest of the inputs.

blocks.title: Maximum
blocks.description: Highest of the inputs.

blocks.title: Average
blocks.description: Average of the inputs.

blocks.title: Absolute value
blocks.description: out = |in|

blocks.title: Limit
blocks.description: Limits the input to [min, max].

blocks.title: Scale (linear)
blocks.description: Linear scaling from [in low, in high] to [out low, out high].

blocks.title: Round
blocks.description: Rounds to the chosen number of decimals.

blocks.title: Formula
blocks.description: Free expression with inputs a…h, e.g. 'a*0.5 + b' or 'sel(a > 20, b, c)'. Functions: abs, min, max, round, sqrt, clamp, sel, floor, ceil, sin, cos, log, exp.

blocks.title: On delay
blocks.description: The output goes on when the input has been on for 'time' seconds.

blocks.title: Off delay
blocks.description: The output goes off 'time' seconds after the input went off.

blocks.title: Pulse
blocks.description: A rising edge gives a pulse of fixed length ('time' seconds).

blocks.title: Pulse generator
blocks.description: Blinks with the chosen on and off time while enabled.

blocks.title: Clock
blocks.description: Local time: hour, minute, minutes since midnight, weekday (1=Mon) and weekend.

blocks.title: Astro clock
blocks.description: The sun's elevation and direction, and whether it is day, from the location in Home Assistant (or your own latitude/longitude). 'day' is on while the sun is above the chosen horizon, and also works with midnight sun and polar night. 'night' is the opposite, e.g. for outdoor lights. 'rise' and 'set' are today's sunrise and sunset in minutes after midnight (like the clock's daymin), -1 if the sun does not rise or set today. Azimuth is degrees from north, clockwise (90 = east, 180 = south). An offset in minutes moves when 'day' starts and ends: 'set ±min' = -30 starts night (outdoor lights on) 30 min before sunset, 'rise ±min' = 30 keeps night until 30 min after sunrise. 'rise' and 'set' still show the real times.

params.name: horizon
params.label: Day while the sun is above

params.name: lat
params.label: Latitude
params.help: Empty = the location in Home Assistant

params.name: lon
params.label: Longitude
params.help: Empty = the location in Home Assistant

blocks.title: Run time
blocks.description: Counts running hours while the input is on. Kept over a restart.

blocks.title: Counter
blocks.description: Counts rising edges. Kept over a restart.

blocks.title: PID controller
blocks.description: General PID controller with anti-windup, for all kinds of processes (temperature, pressure, humidity, CO₂, level, light). Reverse: the output rises when PV is below SP (e.g. heating, humidifying). Direct: the output rises when PV is above SP (e.g. cooling, CO₂ to ventilation). Ti = integral time in seconds (0 = off), Td = derivative time in seconds (the derivative acts on PV and is filtered with Td/10). Enable off gives min out, manual gives the manual value out. The return to automatic is bumpless: the output continues where it was. The bias is added to the output (useful for P-only control or feedforward).

options.label: Reverse: rises when PV < SP (e.g. heating)
Direct: rises when PV > SP (e.g. cooling)

params.name: deadband
params.label: Deadband
params.help: An error within ± the deadband counts as 0, so the output stays still near SP (saves damper and valve actuators). Same unit as PV. 0 = off.

blocks.title: Ramp
blocks.description: The output follows the input with at most 'rate' change per second.

blocks.title: Rate limiter
blocks.description: Limits how fast the output can change: at most 'up' units per second upwards and 'down' per second downwards (0 = unlimited in that direction). When enable is off, the output follows the input directly. 'limiting' is on while the output lags behind. Kept over a restart.

blocks.title: Sample & hold
blocks.description: Holds the value and lets the newest value through at most once per interval (seconds), without a ramp. A change after a quiet period passes at once. Changes smaller than the deadband are not let through. When enable is off, the output follows the input directly. 'updated' is on in the scan the value is let through. Kept over a restart.

blocks.title: Load balancing
blocks.description: Divides the available current (A) between several chargers. Every active charger first gets the minimum current, highest priority first; a charger that cannot get the minimum gets 0 (paused). The rest goes to the highest priority first and is shared evenly between chargers with the same priority, up to each charger's max. The same priority on all gives an even share. 'rest' is current left unused, 'limited' is on when an active charger gets less than its max.

blocks.title: Low-pass filter
blocks.description: First-order filter with time constant tau (seconds).

blocks.title: Multiplexer (MUX)
blocks.description: Outputs the input that index k points to (in0, in1, …). An invalid index is limited to the nearest input and sets err.

blocks.title: Priority select
blocks.description: Outputs the value of the first active priority (g1 highest), otherwise 'else'. Typical: manual > alarm > schedule > auto. idx = active priority (0 = none).

blocks.title: Get bit
blocks.description: Gets one bit (0 = least significant) out of an integer, e.g. a Modbus status word.

blocks.title: Weekly schedule
blocks.description: Time schedule with periods per weekday. q is on in the periods, value gives a value for on/off (e.g. 21/18 °C), next is minutes to the next change. A period whose off time is before its on time runs past midnight. enable = off turns q off (e.g. on a holiday).

blocks.title: Connector (sender)
blocks.description: Sends a signal under a name. Picked up by a “Connector (receiver)” with the same name, on the same page or another one.

blocks.title: Connector (receiver)
blocks.description: Gets the signal from the connector (sender) with the same name.

blocks.title: Macro input
blocks.description: An input on the macro block. The order on the block follows the height on the drawing.

params.name: default
params.label: Default value (when the pin is not connected)

blocks.title: Macro output
blocks.description: An output on the macro block. The order follows the height on the drawing.

blocks.title: KNX send
blocks.description: Sends the value to a KNX group address (knx.send) with the chosen DPT. Sends only on change, with deadband, minimum interval and optional cyclic sending.

blocks.title: KNX listen
blocks.description: Listens for telegrams to a KNX group address (knx_event) and outputs the latest value. 'new' is a pulse when a telegram arrives. Can send a read request on start.

params.name: read_on_start
params.label: Send a read request on start

blocks.title: Modbus write
blocks.description: Writes to a holding register or a coil through HA's Modbus integration (modbus.write_register / write_coil). Raw value = value × scale. Read Modbus values with “Read entity” on a Modbus sensor.
